blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Proprietary language models and their reasoning traces are vulnerable to API-based distillation, where an adversary trains a student model on the teacher model's outputs. To obtain evidence of distillation, model providers can watermark the teacher's outputs, aiming to leave a radioactive signal in the student's outputs. Existing black-box detectors search for such radioactivity using token-level statistics of the suspect model's outputs. However, token-level signals are not always detectable, for instance when the distillation traces are sampled at a low temperature. In this work, we discover the watermark basin, a persistent signal that enables more reliable watermark detection: during fine-tuning, watermarked teacher traces embed a distinct, key-specific geometric signal in parameter space that lies orthogonal to the ordinary task-specific fine-tuning subspace. Building on this, we introduce Watermark Basin Alignment (WM-Basin), a black-box watermark detector that queries the suspect model through its API, without access to its weights or logits. WM-Basin maps generated text to gradient representations using a fixed clean probe model, projects out the ordinary fine-tuning task directions, and tests whether the residual gradient aligns with the watermark basin induced by the watermark key. We evaluate WM-Basin extensively across diverse teacher models and student architectures (from 135M to 8.2B parameters) distilled on mathematical reasoning. At a strict 0.1% false-positive rate, WM-Basin detects 79% of distilled models at n-gram=1 and 45% at n-gram=3, substantially improving over the state-of-the-art token-level baseline (29% and 1.3%, respectively). Because the watermark signal resides in a persistent basin, it survives post-distillation modifications including quantization, pruning, and reinforcement-learning post-training.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Proprietary language models are increasingly targeted by API-based distillation: an adversary queries a closed teacher model and fine-tunes a competing student model on its outputs.
This attack extends black-box model extraction, first demonstrated against ML-as-a-service systems ( Tramèr et al., 2016 ) , and has become a major threat to reasoning LLMs ( Anthropic, 2026a ; Google Threat Intelligence Group, 2026 ; Remler and Hayum, 2026 ) .
Providers have responded by withholding reasoning traces, but concealment does not prevent distillation.
Hidden traces can be extracted at scale from encrypted response blocks ( Panfilov et al., 2026 ) , while answers and short summaries can be expanded into synthetic traces that recover much of the benefit of training on the originals ( Zhang et al., 2026 ) .
Other defenses make extraction harder rather than detectable ( Anthropic, 2026a ; Google Threat Intelligence Group, 2026 ; Savani et al., 2026 ; Ma et al., 2026 ) .
We review related work in full in § 4 .

blocks.en:
In this work, we focus on output watermarking, which is encouraged by emerging regulatory requirements ( European Commission, 2026 ) .
Anthropic, for example, embeds watermarks in texts generated by Claude models released beginning in August 2026 ( Anthropic, 2026b ) .
Such watermarks can survive distillation: Sander et al. (2024) show that students trained on watermarked teacher outputs retain a “radioactive” signal.
Their black-box detector, to our knowledge the only existing one for this setting and our baseline throughout, tests suspect outputs for an excess of watermark-favored tokens, but only where watermark-conditioned contexts recur.
We find that this dependence is fragile: detection degrades sharply with larger context windows and loses most of its power under low-temperature teacher sampling. We therefore seek a watermark signal that does not require exact token-level recurrence.

blocks.en:
Our main finding is the watermark basin : supervised fine-tuning on clean (watermark-free) teacher traces moves a student along a broad task direction , whereas watermarked traces add a faint, key-specific watermark direction (Fig. 1 ), leading the student into a key-specific region of parameter space.
Post-training updates cannot easily push the student out of this basin.
Building on this geometry, we introduce Watermark Basin Alignment ( WM-Basin ) , a black-box detector that represents the suspect model’s outputs and the watermarked teacher’s outputs as gradients of one fixed, clean probe model.
After removing the task subspace estimated from clean models, the distilled student should align with the watermark key more closely than with decoy keys that were never used to watermark the teacher. WM-Basin turns this relative rank into a calibrated p p -value using a non-parametric ranking test ( Dwass, 1957 ) : a small value is evidence that the suspect was distilled from the claimed teacher and key on the audited domain (Fig. 2 ).

We evaluate WM-Basin along many axes: the student architecture, the teacher model, the watermarking scheme, the sampling temperature and watermarked fraction of the distillation traces, the fine-tuning recipe, and the task domain.
Among 1,200 1{,}200 student models distilled from DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-14B ( Guo et al., 2025 ) on OpenR1-Math reasoning traces ( Hugging Face, 2025 ) , at a 0.1 % 0.1\% false-positive rate, WM-Basin detects 79 % 79\% of distilled models at n n -gram = 1 {=}1 and 45 % 45\% at n n -gram = 3 {=}3 , against 29 % 29\% and 1.3 % 1.3\% for the state-of-the-art black-box detector ( Sander et al., 2024 ) .
Quantization, pruning, and reinforcement-learning post-training all leave detection intact, as none of them moves the student out of the watermark basin.
Like any black-box method, WM-Basin reads only the suspect model’s text, so detection depends on that text carrying the teacher’s token distribution.
Continued training on clean data can reshape that distribution and therefore degrade black-box detection, although the basin itself survives in the weights and remains easy to identify under white-box access.
Our contributions are as follows: • Discovery of watermark basins. We find that watermarked distillation places every distilled student in a persistent basin, spanned by the ordinary task direction and a faint, key-specific watermark direction. Leaving this basin without knowledge of the key is difficult: post-training operations (quantization, pruning, supervised fine-tuning, RL) displace weights primarily along the task axis and leave the key-specific component intact, which we exploit for detection. • A parameter-space black-box detector ( WM-Basin ). WM-Basin looks for distillation evidence in parameter space. It maps text outputs to gradients of a fixed clean probe model, removes the shared task subspace, and scores the residual alignment against decoy keys. The watermark becomes far more detectable than in token space, with exact finite-sample false-positive control and no access to the suspect’s parameters. • Robust detection at scale. Across 24 24 student architectures ( 135 135 M to 8.2 8.2 B parameters), 4 4 teachers, and 4 4 watermarking schemes, WM-Basin achieves 79 % 79\% TPR at 0.1 % 0.1\% FPR versus 29 % 29\% for the state-of-the-art token-level detector, and remains effective under quantization, pruning, and RL post-training.

Verifier regime. An audit is opened by the verifier, either the model owner or an authorized third party, and begins by naming one capability the owner sells and the suspect appears to compete on.
We call it the audited domain D D (e.g., math) and let P D P_{D} be its induced prompt distribution; the verifier chooses both and draws every prompt it uses from P D P_{D} .
It holds two disjoint pools: a build pool 𝒳 build \mathcal{X}_{\mathrm{build}} used to construct the detector, and a test pool 𝒳 test \mathcal{X}_{\mathrm{test}} used to read the suspect.
Neither overlaps the adversary’s prompts, which the verifier never sees, and keeping build and test prompts apart avoids score inflation from prompt reuse.
The verifier’s access to ℳ sus \mathcal{M}_{\text{sus}} is black-box : it observes only texts sampled on the test prompts.
The access is also unsupervised in the sense of Sander et al. (2024) : the verifier does not hold the traces ℳ sus \mathcal{M}_{\text{sus}} was trained on, only fresh teacher traces on the build prompts (unwatermarked, watermarked under k ⋆ k^{\star} , and watermarked under M M independent decoy keys k j ← 𝖪𝖾𝗒𝖦𝖾𝗇 k_{j}\leftarrow\mathsf{KeyGen} ), together with a pool of public clean checkpoints.
It knows the system prompts used to query ℳ sus \mathcal{M}_{\text{sus}} and the teacher, because it chooses them, and the number of test prompts sent to the suspect is the query budget.

We evaluate capability on held-out GSM8K ( Cobbe et al., 2021 ) and Math-500 ( Hendrycks et al., 2021 ) ; App. B.2 gives the full distillation setup.

我们评价被搁置的GSM8K(Cobbe等人,2021年)和Math-500(Hendrycks等人,2021年)的能力;App.B.2给出了完整的蒸馏设置.

Detector. WM-Basin turns text into a gradient with a probe model, by default a clean Qwen2.5-3B base warmed on around 450 450 clean teacher traces from the audited domain (App. C.6 studies both the choice of probe and the warm-up).
On 512 512 build-pool prompts we query the teacher under the claimed watermark key and 999 999 decoys, then map those responses and the suspect’s generations through the probe, giving a 1,000 1{,}000 -key reference gradient bank and the suspect gradient scored against it.
Before scoring, we project both away from a PCA task subspace fit on 43 43 off-the-shelf checkpoints, which leaves the key-specific alignment that the rank test reads (§ 2.3 ).
All three stages draw separately from the build pool 𝒳 build \mathcal{X}_{\mathrm{build}} , disjoint from 𝒳 test \mathcal{X}_{\mathrm{test}} .
Ranking the claimed key gives p p -values down to 0.001 0.001 ; unless stated otherwise we report the true positive rate (TPR) at p ≤ 0.01 p{\leq}0.01 , i.e., at a 1 % 1\% false positive rate (FPR).
App. B.6 validates the false positive rate empirically.

在512年512年的建设池中, 我们用声称的水印键和999个诱饵询问老师, 然后通过探测器绘制这些反应和嫌疑人的世代图, 给出1000个1{,}000个基调梯度库,

blocks.en:
Baseline. We compare with the black-box sampled-token detector of Sander et al. (2024) , to our knowledge the only existing detector for this setting.
It reads the same suspect text as WM-Basin , so every comparison is paired.
We run it under its own protocol with both filters that give it power: a position is scored only when its context window occurs in a held-out corpus of 5,000 5{,}000 teacher traces regenerated under the key being scored, and each distinct (context, token) pair is scored once.
Its p p -value is computed analytically from the score’s null distribution rather than by ranking decoys, and we threshold both detectors at the same p p -value.
App. B.4 gives the test used for each watermark scheme and the remaining settings.
blocks.zh:
基线。 我们比较了桑德等人(2024年)的黑盒采样-托肯探测器, 据我们所知,这是这个设定的唯一现有探测器。
它读了与WM-Basin相同的疑似文本,所以每个比较都是对的.
我们用赋予它力量的两种过滤器在自己的协议下运行:只有当上下文窗口出现5000 5{,}000名老师的痕迹在被打的键下重新生成时,方位才会得分,每一对不同的(文字,符牌)都得分一次.

App.B.4给出了每个水印方案和剩余设置所使用的测试.

blocks.en: 3.2 Detection Performance
blocks.zh: 3.2 检测性能

blocks.en:
Effect of the student architecture. Does detection depend on which student architecture the adversary selects?
We vary the student across 24 24 architectures spanning 6 6 families ( 135 135 M to 8.2 8.2 B parameters) and distill 50 50 models per architecture, for 1,200 1{,}200 distilled models per n n -gram window, holding the teacher, distillation recipe, probe model, and reference gradient bank fixed.
Pooled over all architectures (the Overall row of Tab. 1 ), WM-Basin outperforms the baseline at every window and operating point, and at the 5 % 5\% and 1 % 1\% thresholds its margin widens with the window.
At n n -gram = 3 {=}3 and p ≤ 0.001 p{\leq}0.001 , the baseline recovers almost nothing ( 1.3 % 1.3\% ) while WM-Basin detects 45 % 45\% of distilled models.
Detectability is governed by task acquisition rather than architecture: WM-Basin mostly misses students that failed to learn the task, so evading detection means giving up the capability that motivated distillation.
blocks.zh:
学生建筑的影响. 检测是否取决于对手选择哪个学生架构?
我们把学生分成24个24个建筑群,涉及6个家庭(135 135 M 到 8.2 B 参数)和50个模型,每个建筑1,200 1{,}200个模型,每n -gram窗口,持有教师,蒸馏食谱,探测器模型,以及参考梯度库固定。
在所有建筑(Tab 1 的总行)上集合,WM-Basin在每一个窗口和操作点都超过了基线,在5% 5% + 和1% + 1% 的阈值上,它的比值随窗口而扩大。
在n-gram = 3 {=}3 和 p 0.001 p{\leq}0.001时,基线几乎完全恢复(1.3 % 1.3\%),而WM-Basin检测到45%的蒸馏模型.
可探测性受任务获取而非架构的制约:WM-Basin大多想念未能学习任务的学生,因此逃避检测意味着放弃激发蒸馏的能力.

Each cell is the percentage of up to 100 100 distilled models (one per watermark key) flagged at a p p -value threshold of 5 % 5\% , 1 % 1\% , or 0.1 % 0.1\% , i.e., the TPR at that false-positive rate.

Effect of the distillation temperature. What happens when the adversary samples its distillation traces at a temperature the verifier does not know?
We generate the teacher’s traces at T = 1.0 T{=}1.0 , 0.7 0.7 , and 0.5 0.5 and distill 100 100 students from each setting.
A lower T T concentrates the teacher’s output distribution on its most likely tokens.
For WM-Basin , the reference gradient bank remains fixed at T = 1.0 T{=}1.0 , creating a mismatch at the two lower temperatures.
Tab. 2 shows that lowering the distillation temperature costs the black-box baseline most of its power at every window, whereas WM-Basin at p ≤ 0.01 p{\leq}0.01 still flags every suspect at n n -gram = 1 {=}1 and about half of them at n n -gram = 3 {=}3 , even at T = 0.5 T{=}0.5 .
Temperature thus governs what the tokens reveal, not what the gradient reveals : lowering it is a cheap evasion against the baseline but not against WM-Basin .

Effect of the teacher model. Are some teachers harder to protect than others?
We distill the same Qwen2.5-3B student from each of four teachers spanning three families and 8 8 B to 120 120 B parameters: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-14B, gpt-oss-120B ( Agarwal et al., 2025 ) , QwQ-32B ( Team, 2025 ) , and Llama-3.1-8B ( Grattafiori et al., 2024 ) , rebuilding the reference bank for each.
Tab. 3 shows that, at p ≤ 0.05 p\leq 0.05 , WM-Basin detects 96 96 to 100 % 100\% of distilled models for every teacher.
The baseline loses most of its power on two teachers and approaches WM-Basin on the other two.
Its power is thus inherited from the teacher and varies sharply with it, whereas WM-Basin is robust across teachers; App. C.2 relates this to how often each student repeats its contexts.
blocks.zh:
师范模式的效果. 有些老师比其他老师更难保护吗?
我们从四位教师中 分三个家庭 和8个8个B到120个120个B参数中 分别提炼出相同的Quen2.5-3B学生: 深层Seek-R1-Distill-Quen-14B, gpt-oss-120B (Agarwal等人,2025年),QwQ-32B(团队,2025年),和Llama-3.1-8B (Grattafiori等人,2024年),重建每个参考库.
Tab. 3显示,在p 0.05 p\leq 0.05中,WM-Basin检测到96-100%的蒸馏模型,供每个教师使用。
基线在两名教师身上丧失了大部分权力,在其他两名教师身上接近WM-Basin。
因此,它的力量从教师那里继承下来,并且随它而大相径庭,而WM-Basin在教师之间是强有力的;App.C.2将这一点与每个学生重复其背景的频率有关。

Effect of the watermark scheme. Is detection tied to the watermark the teacher happens to deploy?
We replace TextSeal in the teacher’s decoder with GumbelMax ( Aaronson, 2022 ) , KGW ( γ = 0.5 \gamma{=}0.5 ) ( Kirchenbauer et al., 2023 ) , and SynthID ( Dathathri et al., 2024 ) , rebuilding the reference bank for each and distilling 50 50 students per scheme and window.
Tab. 4 shows that all three transfer: WM-Basin flags every student at p ≤ 0.01 p{\leq}0.01 and n n -gram = 1 {=}1 under each scheme, and it outperforms the baseline in every cell, by a margin that widens with the window at p ≤ 0.05 p{\leq}0.05 . WM-Basin needs only traces the teacher generated under a key, not the watermark’s own detection test.
The baseline, in contrast, scores the suspect’s tokens with that test, which must be derived scheme by scheme (App. B.4 ).
To audit a new keyed watermark, the verifier therefore only generates teacher traces under its keys, rebuilds the reference bank, and runs the same detector.
blocks.zh:
水印计划的效果。 检测是否与老师碰巧部署的水印有关?
校对:Soup (Kirchenbauer等人,2023年),以及SynthID(Dathri等人,2024年),重建了每个参考库,并蒸馏了50名每个计划和窗口的学生.
Tab. 4 显示所有三个转校: WM-Basin 旗下每个学生在 0.01 p\leq} 0.01和n-gram = 1 1,它比每个单元格的基线要好,比在p 0.05 p{\leq 时随窗口扩大的差值 0.05 (英语). 校对:Soup
与此相反,基线与这项检验标准对嫌疑人的标志进行评分,而这项检验必须按计划进行(App.B.4)。
为了审计一个新的按键水印,验证器因此只在键下生成教师痕迹,重建参考库,运行同样的探测器.

Effect of the audited domain and system prompt. How close must the audited domain be to the adversary’s distillation data?
We hold the 100 100 suspects fixed and change the domain the verifier audits, from the math domain they were distilled on (OpenR1-Math, MATH, GSM8K) to two domains outside it (code and chat).
For each domain we rebuild the probe warm-up, the task subspace, and both detectors from that domain’s own prompts, none of them the teacher’s training system prompt; App. C.4 lists the exact prompts.
Tab. 5 shows that WM-Basin ’s detection power follows where the suspects were distilled: it ranks every math domain above both non-math ones in every cell, whereas the baseline ranks code above GSM8K at n n -gram = 1 {=}1 and 2 2 .
A hit therefore tells the verifier on which domain the suspect’s text carries the watermark, not only that it carries one; a low score elsewhere means nothing was found there, not that the model is clean.
blocks.zh:
被审计领域和系统的效果迅速。 审计领域必须接近对手的蒸馏数据吗?
我们把100名嫌疑人固定下来,并将核查员审计的范围从数学领域(OpenR1-Math、MATH、GSM8K)转变为外部的两个领域(代码和聊天)。
对于每个域,我们重建了探测器的热身,任务子空间,以及来自域本身的探测器,没有一个是师资培训系统即时的; App. C.4 列出了确切的提示。
Tab. 5显示,WM-Basin的侦测能力跟随嫌疑人的蒸馏地点:它在每个细胞中将每个数学领域都排在两个非磁域之上,而基数序列代码则高于GSM8K,n-gram=1 1和2 2。
因此,打击者告诉核查者嫌疑人的文字在哪个领域带有水印,而不只是它带有水印;在其他地方低分意味着没有找到任何东西,而不是模型是干净的。

Effect of the watermarked fraction and the training recipe. What in the adversary’s data and training recipe lets the watermark reach the student?
At n n -gram = 3 {=}3 we sweep one knob at a time around the default recipe: the watermarked fraction of a fixed 1,900 1{,}900 -trace training set from 1 1 to 100 % 100\% (the remainder filled with clean traces from the same teacher), the distillation LoRA rank r r from 16 16 to 1,024 1{,}024 , and 1 1 , 2 2 , or 3 3 training epochs.
Fig. 4 shows that detection power depends mostly on the watermarked fraction and the LoRA rank, and much less on how long the student trains.
(1) WM-Basin performs at chance when at most 10 % 10\% of the traces are watermarked and exceeds 90 % 90\% TPR once 75 % 75\% are.
(2) Its TPR climbs from 16 % 16\% at r = 16 r{=}16 to 100 % 100\% at r = 512 r{=}512 .
(3) A single epoch already yields 78 % 78\% TPR.
The black-box baseline stays at or below 2 % 2\% at every fraction and reaches its highest value in the figure at the largest rank; WM-Basin outperforms it in every cell of the rank and epoch sweeps.

blocks.en: 3.3 Post-processing and Basin Dynamics
blocks.zh: 3.3 后处理和流域动态

blocks.en:
In § 2.2 , we showed that a watermarked student sits in a narrow basin: a small step along the watermark direction (Eq. ( 1 )) leaves it, while a much larger step along the task direction does not.
We now examine in which direction standard post-processing moves the student, and whether it removes the watermark.

We apply int8, int4, or nf4 quantization, or 10 10 to 30 % 30\% unstructured pruning, to the same 100 100 suspects.

Compression therefore does not move the student out of the watermark basin, and it remains detectable.

Effect of continued SFT and RL. Does continued training on clean data move the distilled model out of its watermark basin?
We continue training the suspects via SFT on cross-domain data and via GRPO ( Shao et al., 2024 ) on verifiable tasks (details in App. D.2 ), holding the probe and the reference bank fixed.
Tab. 7 shows that continued RL leaves the student detectable while continued SFT weakens the signal: WM-Basin detects every distilled model in every GRPO arm at p ≤ 0.05 p{\leq}0.05 and every window, whereas both SFT arms substantially reduce its power.
This ordering matches how far each update moves the model along the watermark direction: SFT on general reasoning traces moves it furthest, SFT on multilingual math less, and GRPO barely at all.
The open-weight detector, teacher-forced on the distillation traces, nevertheless still detects the SFT-trained students.
Continued SFT thus weakens the signal observable in the student’s outputs without moving the model out of the watermark basin.

blocks.en: 4 Related Work
blocks.zh: 4 相关工作

blocks.en:
Model extraction and unauthorized distillation. Frontier providers, threat-intelligence groups, policy analysts, and security researchers now document distillation-oriented misuse in the wild: adversaries harvest reasoning traces at scale from deployed APIs to train competing models ( Anthropic, 2026a ; Google Threat Intelligence Group, 2026 ; Panfilov et al., 2026 ) .
The underlying mechanism is knowledge distillation, which transfers capability from a teacher to a student model ( Hinton et al., 2015 ) .
When exposed through an API, it becomes model extraction : black-box query access alone, without the target’s parameters or training data, suffices to replicate the teacher’s functionality ( Tramèr et al., 2016 ) .
The threat is sharpest for reasoning models, whose step-by-step traces provide dense supervision.
Capability also transfers through synthetic instructions, model-generated reasoning, rubric or reward feedback, and agent trajectories ( Wang et al., 2023 ; Guo et al., 2025 ; Gunjal et al., 2025 ; Zeng et al., 2024 ) .
We study supervised fine-tuning on collected reasoning traces, motivated by evidence that small, high-quality reasoning sets sharply improve students ( Muennighoff et al., 2025 ) .
blocks.zh:
模型提取和未经授权的蒸馏。 边境提供者、威胁情报小组、政策分析人员和安全研究人员现在记录了野外以蒸馏为目的的滥用情况:从部署的API到培训竞争模式的大规模收获推理(Anthropic, 2026a; Google威胁情报组, 2026; Panfilov等人, 2026 ).
基本机制是知识蒸馏,将能力从教师转移到学生模式(Hinton等人,2015年)。
当通过 API 曝光时, 它成为模型提取 : 黑盒查询访问, 没有目标参数或培训数据, 足以复制老师的功能( Tramèr et al., 2016) 。
对于推理模型来说,威胁最尖锐,其逐步的痕迹提供了密集的监督.
能力也通过合成指令,模型生成的推理,rumic或奖励反馈,以及剂轨迹进行转移(Wang等人,2023年;Guo等人,2025年;Gunjal等人,2025年;Zeng等人,2024年).
我们研究对收集的推理痕迹进行有监督的微调,其动机是,有证据表明,小型、高质量的推理集大大改善了学生(Muennighoff等人,2025年)。

blocks.en:
Defenses against extraction. Existing defenses restrict what the API returns, monitor extraction-like querying ( Anthropic, 2026a ; Google Threat Intelligence Group, 2026 ) , or make outputs less useful for training via antidistillation sampling or trace rewriting ( Savani et al., 2026 ; Ma et al., 2026 ) .
Such methods trade away utility for benign users or assume that the attacker stays observable during collection.
That assumption is fragile in practice: adversaries spread collection across many accounts and third-party API resellers, so no single query stream looks like extraction ( Anthropic, 2026a ) .
Detection is complementary: it acts after the fact and leaves the deployed model untouched.
A parallel black-box line, dataset inference ( Maini et al., 2021 ) , resolves ownership by testing whether a suspect shares private knowledge of the victim’s data, without inserting a watermark; it observes that inserted watermarks are off-distribution and therefore not always preserved under stealing.
Classical model watermarking instead hides a signal directly in the weights or via backdoors ( Uchida et al., 2017 ; Adi et al., 2018 ) , read from the parameters or by querying a trigger set; both assume the owner watermarked the suspect model under test, whereas our suspect is a model the owner never trained.
blocks.zh:
防御撤离。 现有防御限制API返回的内容,监控类似提取的查询(Anthropic, 2026a;Google威胁情报组, 2026 ),或者通过抗蒸馏采样或微量重写使输出对训练用处较小(Savani等人, 2026 ; Ma等人, 2026 ).
这种方法为良性用户交换了效用,或假定攻击者在收集过程中仍然可观察到。
这一假设在实践中是脆弱的:对手分散收集到许多账户和第三方API转售商,因此没有一个单一的查询流看起来像提取(Anthropic, 2026a). 。 。 。
侦测是相辅相成的:它事后行动,使部署的模型不受影响。
一条平行的黑框线,数据集推论(Maini等人,2021年),通过测试嫌疑人是否分享对受害人数据的私人知识,而不插入水印来解决所有权问题;它注意到插入的水印是不分配的,因此并不总是在偷窃下保存的.
古典型号的水印直接隐藏在重量上或通过后门的信号(Uchida等人,2017年;Adi等人,2018年),从参数中读取或通过查询触发器集;两者都假设所有者在测试中的疑似型号中标注了水印,而我们的疑似型号则是所有者从未训练过的型号.

blocks.en:
Watermarking and radioactivity. Text watermarking embeds a secret statistical signal into generated text ( Kirchenbauer et al., 2023 ; Kuditipudi et al., 2023 ; Sander et al., 2026 ) .
The idea of tracing data through a trained model originates in computer vision: Sablayrolles et al. (2020) show that imperceptible “radioactive” watermarks in a dataset leave a statistical residue in models trained on it, detectable with a calibrated p p -value even when only 1 % 1\% of the data is marked.
Our rank test follows the same framework. Sander et al. (2024) carry radioactivity over to language models, showing that watermarked distillation leaves a key-specific residue in the student, and others study how well such watermarks survive distillation ( Sander et al., 2026 ; Zhao et al., 2022 ; Pan et al., 2025 ) .
The black-box verifier of Sander et al. (2024) , which counts watermark-favored tokens in a suspect’s sampled text, defines the setting we work in and is, to the best of our knowledge, the only existing method for the task; it is our baseline throughout.
Its limits were not previously characterized, and establishing them is part of our contribution.
The statistic accumulates evidence only where exact watermarked contexts recur, which we show is fragile to wider windows, lower decoding temperatures, and larger text budgets (§ 3.2 , App. C.5 ), the same failure mode that paraphrase attacks exploit against surface-level watermark detection ( Sadasivan et al., 2023 ) . WM-Basin keeps the access level and the generations, and replaces the token statistic with a weight-space one.
blocks.zh:
水印与放射. 文字水印将一个秘密的统计信号嵌入生成的文字(Kirchenbauer等人,2023年;Kuditipudi等人,2023年;Sander等人,2026年)。
通过训练有素的模型追踪数据的想法源于计算机视觉: Sablayroles等人(2020年)表明,在一个数据集中,无法识别的“放射性”水印在对其加以培训的模型中留下了统计残留物,即使只有1%的数据被标出,但用校准的p-值即可检测出来。
我们的军衔测试遵循同样的框架. Sander等人(2024年)将放射性带到语言模型上,表明水印蒸馏在学生中留下一个关键特定的残留物,其他人则研究这种水印在蒸馏中的生存情况(Sander等人,2026年;Zhao等人,2022年;Pan等人,2025年)。
Sander等人(2024年)的黑匣子验证员在嫌疑人的样本文本中计算出有利于水印的标志, 界定了我们的工作环境,
它的局限性以前没有被描述过,确定这些局限性是我们的贡献的一部分。
统计只积累了在具体水标记背景重现时的证据,我们显示这些背景对更大的窗口、较低的解码温度和更大的文本预算(第3.2节,App.C.5)十分脆弱,而后者的失败模式是用来解释攻击对地表水标记检测(Sadasivan等人,2023年)。 WM-Basin保持了访问级别和世代,并以一个权重空间来取代符号统计.

blocks.en:
Weight-space geometry and basins. WM-Basin relies on the fact that students distilled under one key settle into a shared, key-specific region of weight space.
This connects to the geometry of neural loss landscapes: independently trained optima are joined by simple, near-constant-loss curves ( Garipov et al., 2018 ) , and once permutation symmetries are accounted for, the landscape resembles a single wide basin , so separately trained models can be aligned by permutation and merged in weight space ( Ainsworth et al., 2022 ) .
Large language models exhibit the same basin-like structure ( Chen et al., 2026 ; Li et al., 2018 ; Peng et al., 2024 ) . WM-Basin treats the watermark key as carving out one such basin and asks whether a suspect has fallen into it.
blocks.zh:
重量空间几何与盆地. WM-Basin依赖于一个事实,即学生在一个密钥下蒸馏成一个共享的,关键的特殊重量空间.
这与神经失落地貌的几何相连接:独立训练的Ottoima与简单,近恒常的失落曲线结合(Garipov等人,2018年),一旦计算出演化对称性,该地貌类似于一个单一的宽盆地,因此单独训练的模型可以通过演化对齐,并在重量空间中合并(Ainsworth等人,2022年).
大型语言模型表现出相同的盆地状结构(Chen等人,2026年;Li等人,2018年;Peng等人,2024年). WM-Basin将水印键视为刻出一个这样的盆地,并询问疑犯是否落入其中.

blocks.en:
Gradient attribution and representation post-processing. To read this geometric signal from text alone, WM-Basin backpropagates a suspect’s completions through a fixed probe model.
This draws on first-order data attribution: influence functions trace a prediction back to the training points responsible for it using only gradient access ( Koh and Liang, 2017 ) , an idea scaled by gradient tracing ( Pruthi et al., 2020 ) and random-projected attribution ( Park et al., 2023 ) , and adapted to instruction tuning with low-rank projected gradients ( Xia et al., 2024 ) .
Intuitively, a training example’s gradient captures how it would nudge the model, so aligned gradients indicate similar examples.
Raw gradient cosines, however, are dominated by a few shared directions (generic language and formatting): a handful of top components inflate the similarity between otherwise unrelated items ( Ethayarajh, 2019 ; Gao et al., 2019 ; Radovanovic et al., 2010 ; Dinu et al., 2014 ) .
We remove these with an “All-but-the-Top” projection ( Mu et al., 2017 ) , stripping the few dominant yet uninformative directions so that the faint key-specific signal stands out from the generic task geometry.
blocks.zh:
逐步归属和代表后处理. 为了从文字中读取这个几何信号,WM-Basin通过固定的探测模型对嫌疑人的完成进行反射.
这借鉴了一阶数据归属:影响函数追溯到仅使用梯度访问(Koh and Liang, 2017),通过梯度跟踪(Pruti等人, 2020年)和随机预测归属(Park等人, 2023年)来扩展的构想,并适应低阶预测梯度的指令调值(Xia等人, 2024年).
直觉上,一个训练实例的梯度可以捕捉它如何推动模型,因此对齐的梯度可以显示类似的例子.
然而,原始梯度圈以几个共同方向(通用语言和格式化)为主:少数顶端组件会增加原本无关项目的相似性(Ethayarajh, 2019年;Gao等人, 2019年;Radovanovic等人, 2010年;Dinu等人, 2014年)。
我们用“全Top”投影(Mu等人,2017年)去除这些内容, 剥离少数主导但无信息化的方向,

blocks.en: 5 Conclusion and Future Work
blocks.zh: 5. 结论和今后的工作

blocks.en:
In this work, we introduce the watermark basin : distilling on watermarked traces encodes the teacher’s secret key as a faint direction in parameter space, displacing the student’s weights along that key direction and into a region that later training does not easily escape.
Building on this geometry, we design WM-Basin , which reformulates black-box detection of unauthorized distillation from a fragile, surface-level token count into a geometric alignment test in parameter space.
Across a wide range of evaluations, spanning six student families, four teachers, and four watermarking schemes, WM-Basin outperforms the existing baseline by a large margin, and it survives quantization, pruning, and RL post-training.
blocks.zh:
将老师的秘密密钥编码为参数空间的微弱方向, 将学生的权重置于关键方向,
在这个几何学的基础上,我们设计了WM-Basin,它将黑盒检测未经授权的蒸馏从一个脆弱的,表面级的代号计数变为参数空间中的几何校正测试.
通过涵盖6个学生家庭、4个教师和4个水印计划的广泛评价,巴辛河流域的绩效大大超过现有基线,在数量化、循环化和再培训后生存下来。

blocks.en:
Scope and outlook. A watermark can be present in a distilled model but unreadable in its text: continued SFT on clean data suppresses the text-level signal while an open-weight probe still recovers the residual, and a supplementary study (App. D.3 ) finds the same for rewriting the teacher’s traces before distillation. WM-Basin is also an in-domain test: a hit tells the verifier on which domain the suspect’s text carries the watermark, not only that it carries one, and a low score elsewhere means nothing was found there, not that the model is clean (§ 3.2 ).
Both are limits on what a black-box verifier can observe, not on what distillation transfers.
Narrowing the gap between the black-box read and the open-weight probe is thus a promising direction for future work.
blocks.zh:
范围和展望。 水印可以在蒸馏模型中出现,但文本中无法读取:在开量探测器仍能回收残余物的同时,继续使用干净数据的SFT压制文本级信号,补充研究(App. D.3)发现在蒸馏前重写老师的痕迹时同样存在. WM-Basin也是域内测试:一个命中点告诉核查者嫌疑人的文字在哪个域上带有水印,不仅它携带一个,在别处低分意味着在那里没有发现任何东西,而不是模型是干净的(§3.2).
两者都对黑盒核查员能够观察到的事物有限制,而不是对蒸馏转移的事物有限制.
因此,缩小黑箱读数和开量探测数之间的差距是未来工作的有希望的方向。

blocks.en: Ethics Statement
blocks.zh: 道德操守说明

blocks.en:
This work studies whether a model provider can establish, from API access alone, that a suspect model was distilled from its watermarked teacher.
It involves no human subjects and no personal or user data: the distillation corpus (OpenR1-Math-220k), the utility benchmarks (GSM8K and Math-500), and every teacher, student, probe, and clean-pool checkpoint are publicly released artefacts used under their own licenses, and every experiment runs on models we host ourselves.
Because the method produces evidence of provenance, we report how it behaves on models that are not guilty rather than a bare score.
We also measure what weakens the audit, including rewriting the teacher’s traces before distillation, continued fine-tuning, and probing away from the distillation domain.
These are variants of attacks already described in the text-watermarking literature, and we report them because a verifier that does not know the limits of its own test is the more likely harm.
blocks.zh:
这项工作研究了模型提供者是否能够仅从API访问中确定一个可疑模型从其水印教师中蒸馏出来.
它没有涉及人类主题,也没有个人或用户数据:蒸馏器(OpenR1-Math-220k),功用基准(GSM8K和Math-500),每个教师、学生、探测器和清洁池检查站都是根据自己的许可证公开使用的手工艺品,每个实验都以我们自己的模型运行。
因为这个方法能产生出处的证据, 我们报告它如何在模型上表现 无罪而不是赤裸的分数。
我们还衡量削弱审计的因素,包括在蒸馏前重写教师的痕迹,继续微调,以及探索蒸馏领域。
这些是文字标记文献中已经描述的攻击的变体,我们报告这些变体是因为一个不知道自己测试的极限的核查者是最可能的伤害.

blocks.en: Sampled-token baselines. The baselines of Sander et al. (2024) score a single token per position. In the open-weight setting, teacher-forced reading evaluates the student’s top-1 prediction on teacher-generated test text. Their black-box variant scores tokens sampled by the student. We score a token only if its preceding n n -gram appears in held-out teacher text generated with the key being tested. We exclude tokens whose preceding n n -gram also appears in the prompt. Following Sander et al. (2024) , both variants score distinct (context, token) pairs across traces. The open-weight variant additionally requires distinct contexts within each trace.

WM-Basin accumulates evidence monotonically at every window, so more text never costs the verifier anything and no stopping rule is needed: it reaches 100 % 100\% TPR by 0.6 0.6 M tokens at n n -gram 1 1 and 2 2 , and at n n -gram = 3 {=}3 it is within 8 8 points of its ceiling by that budget and spends the twenty times more text that follows gaining the rest.
